title: Golden Retriever Life Expectancy and Weight
text:
This graphic displays 10,000 observations of Golden Retrievers, illustrating how body weight and gender relate to overall life expectancy.
Dogs play an irreplaceable role in human lives, offering loyal companionship, emotional comfort, and unconditional love. Beyond being cherished family members, dogs encourage healthier and more active lifestyles, reduce stress, and frequently serve vital functions as therapy, service, and working partners in our communities.



Cool Facts About Golden Retrievers

Soft Mouth: Goldens have an exceptionally gentle grip, famously capable of carrying a raw egg in their mouths without cracking it.
Water-Repellent Coats: They have a dense double coat designed to repel water and keep them warm when retrieving waterfowl in cold lakes and rivers.
Top-Tier Smarts: Ranked the 4th smartest dog breed, they excel in search-and-rescue, service work, and therapy.
Longevity and Weight: While the average life expectancy for a Golden Retriever is around 10 to 12 years, veterinary studies show that keeping them at a lean, healthy weight can add nearly two years to their lifespan!

title: About
text:
A Golden Retriever


This project investigates the relationship between activity levels, weight, and life expectancy in Golden Retrievers using a dataset of 10,000 observations.
This work was completed as part of Milestone 4 for Bayesian Data Science.

title: Story: The Impact of Daily Activity
text:
When looking at factors influencing a Golden Retriever’s health, diet and weight often get the most attention. However, our dataset of 10,000 dogs reveals another critical factor: daily physical activity.
Golden Retrievers with high activity levels live to an average of 12.2 years, compared to 11.3 years for dogs with low activity levels. Regular walks, fetching, and active playtime provide cardiovascular benefits and joint mobility that appear to add nearly an entire extra year of companionship.
